自建题库/KAPLAN QBANK/ANATOMY/anatomy extra..stem: A 32-year-old woman comes to the physician because of a mass in her left breast. A diagnosis of breast cancer is made and a mastectomy is planned. During the procedure, involvement of the muscle deep to the fatty tissue is seen and a radical mastectomy with removal of the breast, underlying chest muscles, and lymph nodes is performed. Removal of this muscle will most likely compromise which of the following functions?

options.text: Abduction of the humerus at the shoulder
Adduction of the humerus at the shoulder
External rotation of the humerus at the shoulder

自建题库/KAPLAN QBANK/ANATOMY/anatomy extra..explanation: The muscle deep to the breast is the pectoralis major. It adducts and internally rotates the humerus; removing it weakens shoulder adduction. The deltoid (with supraspinatus initiating the movement) abducts the arm; infraspinatus and teres minor externally rotate it; trapezius and rhomboids retract the scapula; biceps brachii and supinator supinate the forearm. The source notes that modified radical mastectomy commonly spares pectoralis major.

choice_explanations.A: Incorrect: shoulder abduction is performed chiefly by deltoid after initiation by supraspinatus.
choice_explanations.B: Correct: pectoralis major adducts and internally rotates the humerus.
choice_explanations.C: Incorrect: infraspinatus and teres minor are the principal external rotators.
choice_explanations.D: Incorrect: trapezius and rhomboids retract the scapula.
choice_explanations.E: Incorrect: biceps brachii and supinator supinate the forearm.

自建题库/KAPLAN QBANK/ANATOMY/anatomy extra..fa_summary: The pectoralis major contributes to humeral adduction; compare shoulder movements with the rotator-cuff actions and arm-movement diagrams.

A.text: Shoulder table: supraspinatus initiates abduction (0–15°), deltoid abducts 15–90°, trapezius and serratus anterior assist above 90°; infraspinatus externally rotates; teres minor externally rotates/adducts; subscapularis internally rotates/adducts.

B.text: No First Aid 2026 page located whose text directly supports this particular option/concept. Do not substitute a merely related index entry or broad chapter heading.

C.text: Shoulder table: supraspinatus initiates abduction (0–15°), deltoid abducts 15–90°, trapezius and serratus anterior assist above 90°; infraspinatus externally rotates; teres minor externally rotates/adducts; subscapularis internally rotates/adducts.

D.text: No First Aid 2026 page located whose text directly supports this particular option/concept. Do not substitute a merely related index entry or broad chapter heading.

E.text: Upper-extremity nerve table: musculocutaneous nerve injury causes loss of forearm flexion and supination, with reduced biceps reflex and lateral forearm sensory loss.

自建题库/KAPLAN QBANK/ANATOMY/anatomy extra..stem: A 59-year-old man is brought to the emergency department after being found unconscious by his wife. On examination, he is unable to move his extremities and has decerebrate posturing. The patient is unable to speak or move his face. He is able to answer yes/no questions by using eye blinks or vertical eye movements, but has no horizontal eye movements. He is unable to move his limbs in response to commands and has upgoing plantar responses bilaterally. Pathology of which of the following vessels is most likely responsible for this patient's condition?
自建题库/KAPLAN QBANK/ANATOMY/anatomy extra..explanation: This is locked-in syndrome from a bilateral lesion of the ventral pons, classically caused by basilar artery occlusion. The patient is conscious and retains vertical eye movements and blinking but has quadriplegia and loss of most voluntary motor output. AICA, PICA, and vertebral artery lesions more typically produce focal/lateral brainstem or cerebellar syndromes; an MCA lesion causes a hemispheric rather than bilateral ventral pontine syndrome.

choice_explanations.A: Incorrect: AICA infarction classically affects lateral caudal pons and may cause facial findings, not the described bilateral ventral pontine syndrome.
choice_explanations.B: Correct: basilar artery supplies the ventral pons bilaterally; occlusion can cause locked-in syndrome.
choice_explanations.C: Incorrect: MCA occlusion causes a cerebral hemispheric syndrome, usually with contralateral deficits.
choice_explanations.D: Incorrect: PICA occlusion classically causes lateral medullary syndrome.
choice_explanations.E: Incorrect: vertebral artery disease can cause medullary/posterior-circulation findings but is not the classic vessel for bilateral ventral pontine locked-in syndrome.

自建题库/KAPLAN QBANK/ANATOMY/anatomy extra..fa_summary: Basilar artery occlusion can injure pontine corticospinal/corticobulbar tracts, causing quadriplegia and loss of voluntary facial, mouth, and tongue movement; vertical eye movements may remain intact in locked-in syndrome.

A.text: Stroke table: basilar artery lesions involve pons/medulla/lower midbrain and can produce quadriplegia, preserved blinking/vertical eye movements, and locked-in syndrome; ACA/MCA/AICA patterns are contrasted on this page.

B.text: Stroke table: basilar artery lesions involve pons/medulla/lower midbrain and can produce quadriplegia, preserved blinking/vertical eye movements, and locked-in syndrome; ACA/MCA/AICA patterns are contrasted on this page.

C.text: Stroke table: basilar artery lesions involve pons/medulla/lower midbrain and can produce quadriplegia, preserved blinking/vertical eye movements, and locked-in syndrome; ACA/MCA/AICA patterns are contrasted on this page.

D.text: Stroke table: PICA infarction causes lateral medullary (Wallenberg) syndrome; vertebral artery involvement is noted in medial medullary syndrome.

E.text: Stroke table: PICA infarction causes lateral medullary (Wallenberg) syndrome; vertebral artery involvement is noted in medial medullary syndrome.

自建题库/KAPLAN QBANK/ANATOMY/anatomy extra..stem: A 21-year-old man is bitten by a stray cat. The wound becomes erythematous and swollen despite appropriate wound care. Five days later, the patient notices a pustule at the wound site that was not previously present and develops a low-grade fever. His symptoms persist, and two weeks later, he complains of pain in the back of his leg. Physical examination reveals a swollen, tender lymph node in the popliteal fossa. An infected cat bite in which of the following sites would most likely induce lymphadenopathy in this region?

options.text: Lateral side of the dorsum of the foot
Medial side of the leg below the knee
Medial side of the sole of the foot

自建题库/KAPLAN QBANK/ANATOMY/anatomy extra..explanation: Most superficial lymph from the lower limb follows the great saphenous vein to superficial inguinal nodes. The important exception is the lateral dorsum of the foot, whose lymph follows the small saphenous vein to popliteal nodes. Thus infection at option A can produce popliteal lymphadenopathy. The source also identifies the presentation as cat-scratch disease due to Bartonella henselae.

choice_explanations.A: Correct: lateral dorsum of the foot drains with the small saphenous pathway to popliteal nodes.
choice_explanations.B: Incorrect: superficial lymph from the thigh generally drains to superficial inguinal nodes.
choice_explanations.C: Incorrect: the medial leg follows the great saphenous pathway to superficial inguinal nodes.
choice_explanations.D: Incorrect: medial foot/sole drainage generally reaches superficial inguinal nodes via the great saphenous pathway.
choice_explanations.E: Incorrect: medial thigh drains to superficial inguinal nodes.

自建题库/KAPLAN QBANK/ANATOMY/anatomy extra..fa_summary: First Aid 2026 does not directly cover the superficial lymphatic drainage route tested here; no unrelated page number is assigned.

A.text: Lymphatic drainage table: superficial inguinal nodes receive most skin below the umbilicus, except the popliteal area; popliteal nodes drain dorsolateral foot and posterior calf. The page notes medial foot/leg cellulitis with superficial inguinal drainage.

B.text: Lymphatic drainage table: superficial inguinal nodes receive most skin below the umbilicus, except the popliteal area; popliteal nodes drain dorsolateral foot and posterior calf. The page notes medial foot/leg cellulitis with superficial inguinal drainage.

C.text: Lymphatic drainage table: superficial inguinal nodes receive most skin below the umbilicus, except the popliteal area; popliteal nodes drain dorsolateral foot and posterior calf. The page notes medial foot/leg cellulitis with superficial inguinal drainage.

D.text: Lymphatic drainage table: superficial inguinal nodes receive most skin below the umbilicus, except the popliteal area; popliteal nodes drain dorsolateral foot and posterior calf. The page notes medial foot/leg cellulitis with superficial inguinal drainage.

E.text: Lymphatic drainage table: superficial inguinal nodes receive most skin below the umbilicus, except the popliteal area; popliteal nodes drain dorsolateral foot and posterior calf. The page notes medial foot/leg cellulitis with superficial inguinal drainage.

自建题库/KAPLAN QBANK/ANATOMY/anatomy extra..stem: A 50-year-old man who is an electrician comes to the physician because of recent onset pain and tingling in his left arm. Neurologic examination shows absence of sensation to light touch and pinprick on the fourth and fifth digits of his left hand and his medial forearm. There is also clawing of all digits of the left hand. Rotating the patient's head to the left side with the neck extended results in loss of the radial pulse on the left. An x-ray of the neck shows a cervical rib. Which of the following structures is most likely being compressed?

options.text: C6 root of the brachial plexus
Lower trunk of the brachial plexus
Medial cord of the brachial plexus
Upper trunk of the brachial plexus

自建题库/KAPLAN QBANK/ANATOMY/anatomy extra..explanation: A cervical rib can narrow the thoracic outlet and compress the lower trunk of the brachial plexus (predominantly C8-T1), causing sensory symptoms along the medial hand/forearm and intrinsic-hand weakness or clawing. Positional loss of the radial pulse indicates associated compression of the subclavian artery. A peripheral ulnar nerve lesion would not explain medial forearm sensory loss or the vascular finding.

choice_explanations.A: Incorrect: C6 root involvement would not match the C8-T1-predominant medial hand findings.
choice_explanations.B: Incorrect: long thoracic nerve injury weakens serratus anterior and causes scapular winging, not this sensory pattern.
choice_explanations.C: Correct: lower-trunk compression explains C8-T1 sensory and intrinsic-hand motor deficits in thoracic outlet syndrome.
choice_explanations.D: Incorrect: medial cord lesions can affect medial arm/hand nerves but the classic cervical-rib compression is at the lower trunk.
choice_explanations.E: Incorrect: ulnar neuropathy does not affect medial forearm sensation and cannot explain the positional pulse loss.
choice_explanations.F: Incorrect: upper-trunk lesions typically affect C5-C6 distribution.

自建题库/KAPLAN QBANK/ANATOMY/anatomy extra..fa_summary: Thoracic outlet compression can affect the lower brachial-plexus trunk (C8–T1); a cervical/anomalous first rib is a recognized cause.

A.text: Brachial-plexus lesions table/diagram: upper trunk C5–C6 injury (Erb palsy) weakens biceps flexion/supination; lower trunk C8–T1 injury (Klumpke) affects intrinsic hand muscles and may cause claw hand; thoracic outlet syndrome compresses lower trunk and subclavian vessels; long thoracic C5–C7 injury affects serratus anterior and causes scapular winging/inability to anchor the scapula. This supports the scapular motor-deficit option; the page does not use the exact word ‘protraction.’

B.text: Brachial-plexus lesions table/diagram: upper trunk C5–C6 injury (Erb palsy) weakens biceps flexion/supination; lower trunk C8–T1 injury (Klumpke) affects intrinsic hand muscles and may cause claw hand; thoracic outlet syndrome compresses lower trunk and subclavian vessels; long thoracic C5–C7 injury affects serratus anterior and causes scapular winging/inability to anchor the scapula. This supports the scapular motor-deficit option; the page does not use the exact word ‘protraction.’

This supports the scapular motor-deficit option; the page does not use the exact word ‘protraction.’

D.text: Brachial-plexus lesions table/diagram: upper trunk C5–C6 injury (Erb palsy) weakens biceps flexion/supination; lower trunk C8–T1 injury (Klumpke) affects intrinsic hand muscles and may cause claw hand; thoracic outlet syndrome compresses lower trunk and subclavian vessels; long thoracic C5–C7 injury affects serratus anterior and causes scapular winging/inability to anchor the scapula. This supports the scapular motor-deficit option; the page does not use the exact word ‘protraction.’

E.text: Upper-extremity nerve table: ulnar neuropathy causes ulnar claw, impaired finger abduction/adduction, and sensory loss over the ulnar 1½ fingers including the hypothenar eminence.

This supports the scapular motor-deficit option; the page does not use the exact word ‘protraction.’

自建题库/KAPLAN QBANK/ANATOMY/anatomy extra..stem: A 17-year-old boy is brought to the emergency department because of several stab wounds he sustained in a gang fight. Physical examination shows a 3-cm penetrating wound on the posterolateral aspect of the neck that has partially severed the C6 ventral ramus as it emerges through the scalene interval. The patient says he has pain in the region of the wound and there is significant bruising in this area. Which of the following additional findings will most likely be seen in this patient?

options.text: Anesthesia in skin covering the hypothenar eminence
Weakness in the ability to protract the scapula

自建题库/KAPLAN QBANK/ANATOMY/anatomy extra..explanation: The long thoracic nerve is formed by contributions from C5-C7 ventral rami and innervates serratus anterior. Injury involving C6 root contributions can weaken serratus anterior, impairing scapular protraction and potentially causing winging. The other options point to ulnar, vagal/recurrent laryngeal, median, or lower-root/median-ulnar functions, respectively.

choice_explanations.A: Incorrect: hypothenar skin sensation is supplied by the ulnar nerve, predominantly lower plexus fibers.
choice_explanations.B: Incorrect: hoarseness suggests laryngeal/vagus or recurrent laryngeal nerve involvement.
choice_explanations.C: Incorrect: thenar muscles are chiefly supplied by the recurrent median nerve, with substantial C8-T1 contribution.
choice_explanations.D: Correct: long thoracic nerve (C5-C7 roots) supplies serratus anterior, which protracts and stabilizes the scapula.
choice_explanations.E: Incorrect: thumb flexion is chiefly via anterior interosseous/median and ulnar-innervated muscles with lower-root contributions.

自建题库/KAPLAN QBANK/ANATOMY/anatomy extra..fa_summary: The long thoracic nerve arises from C5–C7 ventral rami and innervates serratus anterior; injury can cause winged scapula and impaired scapular stabilization.

A.text: Upper-extremity nerve table: ulnar neuropathy causes ulnar claw, impaired finger abduction/adduction, and sensory loss over the ulnar 1½ fingers including the hypothenar eminence.

B.text: No First Aid 2026 page located whose text directly supports this particular option/concept. Do not substitute a merely related index entry or broad chapter heading.

C.text: The hand-distortion section notes that thenar eminence atrophy can be seen in median-nerve lesions, while hypothenar eminence atrophy can be seen in ulnar-nerve lesions.

D.text: Brachial-plexus lesions table/diagram: upper trunk C5–C6 injury (Erb palsy) weakens biceps flexion/supination; lower trunk C8–T1 injury (Klumpke) affects intrinsic hand muscles and may cause claw hand; thoracic outlet syndrome compresses lower trunk and subclavian vessels; long thoracic C5–C7 injury affects serratus anterior and causes scapular winging/inability to anchor the scapula. This supports the scapular motor-deficit option; the page does not use the exact word ‘protraction.’

E.text: Hand-muscle table: thenar muscles include thumb flexors; dorsal interossei abduct and palmar interossei adduct fingers; the page includes the carpal-tunnel contents and hand-muscle figures.

自建题库/KAPLAN QBANK/ANATOMY/anatomy extra..stem: A 68-year-old man with a history of hypertension is admitted to the intensive care unit after sustaining a stroke. He describes recent onset dizziness and difficulty standing upright without falling over. Physical examination shows loss of pain and temperature sensation on the right side of the face and the left side of the body. The right eye exhibits partial ptosis and pupillary miosis. He is discharged 6 days later and is transferred to a rehabilitation center. A more comprehensive physical examination also reveals difficulty in elevating the tongue to the roof of the mouth. Dysfunction of which of the following muscles is most likely responsible for this finding in this patient?
自建题库/KAPLAN QBANK/ANATOMY/anatomy extra..explanation: The crossed face/body sensory findings, ipsilateral Horner syndrome, and ataxia indicate lateral medullary (Wallenberg) syndrome. Involvement of nucleus ambiguus/pharyngeal motor pathways can impair palatoglossus, which elevates the posterior tongue and is supplied through the vagus nerve via the pharyngeal plexus. Tensor veli palatini is supplied by V3; the other listed muscles have different actions/innervation.

choice_explanations.A: Incorrect: buccinator compresses the cheek and is supplied by facial nerve.
choice_explanations.B: Incorrect: geniohyoid elevates/anteriorly draws the hyoid and is supplied by C1 fibers traveling with hypoglossal nerve.
choice_explanations.C: Correct: palatoglossus elevates the posterior tongue and receives vagal motor innervation via the pharyngeal plexus.
choice_explanations.D: Incorrect: palatopharyngeus elevates the pharynx and larynx during swallowing; it is vagally innervated but does not primarily elevate the tongue.
choice_explanations.E: Incorrect: tensor veli palatini tenses the soft palate and is supplied by mandibular division of CN V.

自建题库/KAPLAN QBANK/ANATOMY/anatomy extra..fa_summary: Lateral medullary syndrome can damage nucleus ambiguus pathways; CN IX/X involvement causes dysphagia and related palatal/pharyngeal deficits.

B.text: No First Aid 2026 page located whose text directly supports this particular option/concept. Do not substitute a merely related index entry or broad chapter heading.

C.text: Tongue-innervation section: CN X supplies palatoglossus, which elevates the posterior tongue during swallowing; CN XII supplies other listed tongue muscles.

自建题库/KAPLAN QBANK/ANATOMY/anatomy extra..stem: A 24-year-old man who is a truck driver is brought to the emergency department because of a fracture of the right humerus. Physical examination shows an inability to extend the right hand at the wrist. The patient can flex all of the fingers but he cannot make a tight fist with the right hand. Which of the following nerves is most likely injured as a result of this fracture?
自建题库/KAPLAN QBANK/ANATOMY/anatomy extra..explanation: A midshaft humeral fracture can injure the radial nerve in the radial (spiral) groove, causing wrist drop from loss of wrist-extensor function. Finger flexors may remain intact, but wrist extension stabilizes the wrist and is needed to generate a strong fist. The nerve travels with the profunda brachii vessels in the groove.

choice_explanations.A: Incorrect: axillary injury weakens deltoid/teres minor and shoulder abduction/external rotation.
choice_explanations.B: Incorrect: medial brachial cutaneous nerve is sensory and does not extend the wrist.
choice_explanations.C: Incorrect: median injury weakens many forearm flexors and thenar muscles, not the characteristic wrist extensors affected here.
choice_explanations.D: Incorrect: musculocutaneous injury weakens elbow flexion and forearm supination.
choice_explanations.E: Correct: radial nerve injury at the humeral shaft causes wrist drop.

自建题库/KAPLAN QBANK/ANATOMY/anatomy extra..fa_summary: A midshaft humerus fracture can injure the radial nerve and cause wrist drop; loss of wrist extension also reduces grip strength.

A.text: Upper-extremity nerve table: axillary nerve injury is associated with surgical-neck fracture and loss of arm abduction beyond 15 degrees; deltoid/lateral-arm sensory findings are noted.

B.text: No First Aid 2026 page located whose text directly supports this particular option/concept. Do not substitute a merely related index entry or broad chapter heading.

C.text: Upper-extremity nerve table: median nerve injury can cause thenar/LOAF deficits and sensory loss involving the lateral 3½ fingers; carpal tunnel syndrome is a distal median-nerve lesion.

D.text: Upper-extremity nerve table: musculocutaneous nerve injury causes loss of forearm flexion and supination, with reduced biceps reflex and lateral forearm sensory loss.

E.text: Upper-extremity nerve table: midshaft humeral fracture may injure radial nerve and cause wrist drop; wrist extension is needed for maximal grip strength.

自建题库/KAPLAN QBANK/ANATOMY/anatomy extra..stem: A 56-year-old man with a history of chronic hypertension comes to the physician because of recent onset of palpitations. He says that he particularly notices the palpitations when he lacks sleep or drinks too much caffeine. Physical examination shows a heart rhythm that is irregularly irregular but there is no evidence of murmurs or gallops. ECG reveals absent P waves. The patient is started on a beta blocker. Three months later, the patient arrives in the emergency department after acute onset weakness and lethargy. CT scan reveals no hemorrhage but diffusion-weighted MRI reveals evidence of ischemic stroke. Absent blood flow to which of the following arteries is most likely to produce the greatest amount of ischemic damage?

options.text: Anterior cerebral artery at its origin from the internal carotid artery
Middle cerebral artery at its origin from the internal carotid artery
Posterior cerebral artery at its origin from the basilar artery

自建题库/KAPLAN QBANK/ANATOMY/anatomy extra..explanation: Atrial fibrillation predisposes to cardioembolic ischemic stroke. Among the listed vessels, the middle cerebral artery is not part of the arterial ring of the circle of Willis and has no equivalent collateral route around an occlusion at its origin; it supplies much of the lateral cerebral hemisphere. Occlusion at the specified origin therefore risks extensive ischemia. The communicating arteries and ACA/PCA are components of the circle and can participate in collateral flow.

choice_explanations.A: Incorrect: ACA is part of the circle of Willis and may receive collateral flow through the anterior communicating artery.
choice_explanations.B: Incorrect: the anterior communicating artery is itself a collateral connection.
choice_explanations.C: Correct: MCA is not part of the circle of Willis and supplies a large lateral cortical territory.
choice_explanations.D: Incorrect: PCA is connected to the circle through the posterior communicating artery.
choice_explanations.E: Incorrect: posterior communicating artery is a collateral link between internal carotid and posterior cerebral circulations.

自建题库/KAPLAN QBANK/ANATOMY/anatomy extra..fa_summary: The Circle of Willis provides collateral routes between anterior and posterior cerebral circulations; the middle cerebral artery is outside the ring and supplies the lateral hemisphere.

自建题库/KAPLAN QBANK/ANATOMY/anatomy extra..stem: A 35-year-old pregnant woman at 32 weeks' gestation comes to the physician because of pain and tingling in her hands. She also says that at times her hands feel numb; however, she cannot pinpoint exactly where the numbness is centered. She reports no issues with her pregnancy. Physical examination shows wasting of the thenar eminence. Physical examination will most likely also reveal loss of sensation in which of the following sites?

options.text: Dorsal aspect of the hand (not fingers) on the medial side
Dorsal aspect of the hand (not fingers) on the lateral side
Dorsal aspect of the proximal part of the forefinger
Dorsal aspect of the proximal part of the thumb
Nail bed of the third digit

自建题库/KAPLAN QBANK/ANATOMY/anatomy extra..explanation: Pregnancy-associated fluid retention can promote carpal tunnel syndrome, compressing the median nerve beneath the flexor retinaculum. Thenar wasting supports median neuropathy. Sensation at the distal palmar fingertips and nail beds of the lateral 3½ digits is carried by palmar digital branches of the median nerve; the dorsal proximal hand is largely supplied by superficial radial or ulnar branches, while dorsal distal phalanges are an exception and receive median/ulnar digital supply.

choice_explanations.A: Incorrect: medial dorsal hand is supplied primarily by the dorsal cutaneous branch of the ulnar nerve.
choice_explanations.B: Incorrect: lateral dorsal hand, except distal digit tips, is supplied by the superficial radial nerve.
choice_explanations.C: Incorrect: proximal dorsal index finger is supplied by the superficial radial nerve.
choice_explanations.D: Incorrect: proximal dorsal thumb is supplied by the superficial radial nerve.
choice_explanations.E: Correct: the third digit nail bed is supplied by the median nerve's digital branches.

自建题库/KAPLAN QBANK/ANATOMY/anatomy extra..fa_summary: Median nerve compression in carpal tunnel syndrome causes thenar weakness/atrophy and sensory symptoms in the lateral digits; the palmar cutaneous branch travels outside the tunnel, sparing thenar skin sensation.

A.text: Labeled palm/dorsum hand-innervation diagram identifies radial, median, and ulnar sensory territories and labels the medial brachial and antebrachial cutaneous nerves.

B.text: Labeled palm/dorsum hand-innervation diagram identifies radial, median, and ulnar sensory territories and labels the medial brachial and antebrachial cutaneous nerves.

C.text: Labeled palm/dorsum hand-innervation diagram identifies radial, median, and ulnar sensory territories and labels the medial brachial and antebrachial cutaneous nerves.

D.text: Labeled palm/dorsum hand-innervation diagram identifies radial, median, and ulnar sensory territories and labels the medial brachial and antebrachial cutaneous nerves.

E.text: Upper-extremity nerve table: median nerve injury can cause thenar/LOAF deficits and sensory loss involving the lateral 3½ fingers; carpal tunnel syndrome is a distal median-nerve lesion.

自建题库/KAPLAN QBANK/ANATOMY/anatomy extra..stem: A 12-year-old girl is brought to the physician because of a severe sore throat. She describes significant pain with swallowing and general feelings of malaise. Her parents report that the patient has had a high fever for the past several days. Physical examination shows an erythematous patch on the upper posterior pharynx and tenderness of the cervical lymph nodes. Her temperature is 39.5°C (103.1°F). The nerve responsible for this patient's throat pain is also involved in which of the following functions?

options.text: Sensory input from carotid sinus baroreceptors
Taste in the anterior two-thirds of the tongue

自建题库/KAPLAN QBANK/ANATOMY/anatomy extra..explanation: Pain from the posterior pharynx is carried in part by glossopharyngeal nerve (CN IX). CN IX also carries afferent information from the carotid sinus baroreceptors (and carotid body chemoreceptors). The other choices correspond chiefly to spinal accessory, hypoglossal, mandibular trigeminal, and facial nerves, respectively.

choice_explanations.A: Incorrect: contralateral head rotation is produced by sternocleidomastoid, supplied by CN XI.
choice_explanations.B: Incorrect: intrinsic tongue muscles are supplied by CN XII.
choice_explanations.C: Incorrect: lower-jaw sensation is carried by mandibular division of CN V.
choice_explanations.D: Correct: CN IX carries carotid sinus baroreceptor afferents.
choice_explanations.E: Incorrect: taste from the anterior two-thirds of the tongue is carried by chorda tympani (CN VII).

自建题库/KAPLAN QBANK/ANATOMY/anatomy extra..fa_summary: Carotid sinus baroreceptor afferents travel in CN IX to the nucleus tractus solitarius; aortic arch afferents travel in CN X.

A.text: Cranial-nerve table: CN IX monitors carotid body/sinus chemo- and baroreceptors; CN XI turns the head; CN XII moves the tongue; CN V carries facial/lower-jaw sensation; CN VII carries anterior-tongue taste and closes the eye; CN X supports talking and swallowing.

B.text: Cranial-nerve table: CN IX monitors carotid body/sinus chemo- and baroreceptors; CN XI turns the head; CN XII moves the tongue; CN V carries facial/lower-jaw sensation; CN VII carries anterior-tongue taste and closes the eye; CN X supports talking and swallowing.

A single-photon emission computed tomography (SPECT) image using technetium (Tc)-labeled red blood cells is shown. Greater blood flow is indicated by orange to red colors and poor blood flow is indicated by blue or lack of signal. Which of the following structures shows an abnormal blood-perfusion pattern according to this imaging study?
自建题库/KAPLAN QBANK/ANATOMY/anatomy extra..explanation: The SPECT image shows marked asymmetry, with reduced signal in the right transverse sinus (displayed on the left side of the image). The source identifies the transverse sinus as the abnormal structure. choice_explanations.A: Incorrect: the source explanation identifies the transverse sinus, not the inferior sagittal sinus.
choice_explanations.B: Incorrect: the image finding described in the source is not the internal jugular vein.

choice_explanations.D: Incorrect: the source localizes the perfusion asymmetry to a dural venous sinus, not the PCA.
choice_explanations.E: Incorrect: the source identifies the transverse sinus rather than the superior sagittal sinus.
choice_explanations.F: Correct: the right transverse sinus shows markedly decreased signal in the supplied image.

自建题库/KAPLAN QBANK/ANATOMY/anatomy extra..stem: A 29-year-old woman comes to the physician for a follow-up examination because of increasing pain in her right eye. She had recently been diagnosed with severe optic neuritis in her right eye. Her past neurologic history is significant for weakness in her right leg 2 years ago that resolved spontaneously. She also reports some tingling in her left hand 5 years ago, which also resolved without treatment. The physician tests her pupillary response by shining a light in her right eye and in her left eye. Which of the following findings is most likely in this patient?

options.text: Pattern A in the pupil-response table
Pattern B in the pupil-response table
Pattern C in the pupil-response table
Pattern D in the pupil-response table
Pattern E in the pupil-response table
Pattern F in the pupil-response table

自建题库/KAPLAN QBANK/ANATOMY/anatomy extra..explanation: The history is consistent with multiple sclerosis and right optic neuritis causing a right afferent pupillary defect. Light in the affected right eye produces no direct or consensual response because the afferent limb is interrupted. Light in the intact left eye still activates both efferent pathways, so both pupils constrict. This is pattern F.

choice_explanations.A: Incorrect: describes absent responses when light enters the left eye instead.
choice_explanations.B: Incorrect: predicts a response to light in the affected right eye and an intact response to light in the left eye.
choice_explanations.C: Incorrect: predicts a response in the right pupil when light is shone in the affected right eye.
choice_explanations.D: Incorrect: predicts preserved left-pupil constriction with right-eye illumination, inconsistent with right afferent failure.
choice_explanations.E: Incorrect: predicts a normal left-eye afferent response in the left pupil but no right-pupil response; the intact left afferent input should constrict both pupils.
choice_explanations.F: Correct: no responses with right-eye illumination; both pupils constrict with left-eye illumination.

自建题库/KAPLAN QBANK/ANATOMY/anatomy extra..fa_summary: Multiple sclerosis causes CNS demyelination with neurologic deficits separated in time and space; optic neuritis is a common presentation. A unilateral optic-nerve lesion causes an afferent pupillary defect: illumination of the affected eye fails to constrict either pupil, while illumination of the unaffected eye constricts both.

自建题库/KAPLAN QBANK/ANATOMY/anatomy extra..stem: A 26-year-old woman has worked out twice a week for several months at a local exercise club. Recently she developed severe weakness in abduction of her thighs against resistance using an exercise machine. It is determined that this weakness began soon after she received an intramuscular injection of a vaccine. Damage to which of the following nerves is most likely responsible for this loss of function?
自建题库/KAPLAN QBANK/ANATOMY/anatomy extra..explanation: Hip abduction is performed chiefly by gluteus medius and minimus, supplied by the superior gluteal nerve (L4-S1). A misplaced intragluteal injection can injure this nerve. The femoral nerve mainly supplies anterior thigh muscles; obturator nerve supplies most medial thigh adductors; deep fibular and tibial nerves supply leg compartments.

choice_explanations.A: Incorrect: deep fibular nerve supplies anterior leg dorsiflexors and toe extensors.
choice_explanations.B: Incorrect: femoral nerve supplies anterior thigh muscles and supports hip flexion/knee extension.
choice_explanations.C: Incorrect: obturator nerve supplies thigh adductors, not the principal abductors.
choice_explanations.D: Correct: superior gluteal nerve supplies gluteus medius and minimus, the principal hip abductors.
choice_explanations.E: Incorrect: tibial nerve supplies posterior leg and plantar foot muscles.

A.text: Lower-extremity nerve table: deep peroneal nerve supplies anterior-compartment dorsiflexors; tibial nerve supplies posterior-leg/foot muscles; superior gluteal nerve supplies gluteus medius/minimus and tensor fascia lata, with injection injury causing Trendelenburg findings.

B.text: Lower-extremity nerve table: obturator nerve supplies medial-thigh adductors and medial-thigh sensation; femoral nerve supplies quadriceps and supports knee extension.

C.text: Lower-extremity nerve table: obturator nerve supplies medial-thigh adductors and medial-thigh sensation; femoral nerve supplies quadriceps and supports knee extension.

D.text: Lower-extremity nerve table: deep peroneal nerve supplies anterior-compartment dorsiflexors; tibial nerve supplies posterior-leg/foot muscles; superior gluteal nerve supplies gluteus medius/minimus and tensor fascia lata, with injection injury causing Trendelenburg findings.

E.text: Lower-extremity nerve table: deep peroneal nerve supplies anterior-compartment dorsiflexors; tibial nerve supplies posterior-leg/foot muscles; superior gluteal nerve supplies gluteus medius/minimus and tensor fascia lata, with injection injury causing Trendelenburg findings.

自建题库/KAPLAN QBANK/ANATOMY/anatomy extra..fa_summary: First Aid lists gluteus medius/minimus as hip abductors (p. 455) and identifies their superior gluteal nerve supply, injection injury, and Trendelenburg gait (p. 456).

自建题库/KAPLAN QBANK/ANATOMY/anatomy extra..stem: A 33-year-old woman is brought to the emergency department after a skiing accident. She tells the physician that she was going too fast and grabbed a tree with her right arm to avoid colliding with another skier. Following the injury, the patient complained of weakness and numbness in her right upper extremity. Physical examination shows pain and numbness in the medial two fingers, the medial aspect of the palm, and in the medial aspect of the arm and forearm on the right. Examination also reveals clawing of digits II-V on the right hand. This patient most likely injured which of the following?

options.text: The lower trunk of the brachial plexus
The upper trunk of the brachial plexus

自建题库/KAPLAN QBANK/ANATOMY/anatomy extra..explanation: Traction on an abducted arm while grabbing a fixed object can injure the lower trunk of the brachial plexus (C8-T1, Klumpke pattern). Medial hand/forearm sensory loss and intrinsic-hand weakness with clawing support lower-trunk injury. A single ulnar nerve lesion would not explain medial forearm sensory change or the broad hand findings.

choice_explanations.A: Incorrect: axillary injury affects deltoid/teres minor and lateral shoulder sensation.
choice_explanations.B: Correct: lower-trunk traction injury causes C8-T1 deficits and intrinsic-hand weakness/clawing.
choice_explanations.C: Incorrect: median neuropathy does not explain medial forearm sensory loss and the full described distribution.
choice_explanations.D: Incorrect: radial neuropathy primarily affects extension and dorsal radial sensation.
choice_explanations.E: Incorrect: ulnar neuropathy can cause clawing but not medial forearm sensory loss.
choice_explanations.F: Incorrect: upper-trunk injury produces C5-C6 deficits, classically Erb palsy.

A.text: Upper-extremity nerve table: axillary nerve injury is associated with surgical-neck fracture and loss of arm abduction beyond 15 degrees; deltoid/lateral-arm sensory findings are noted.

B.text: Brachial-plexus lesions table/diagram: upper trunk C5–C6 injury (Erb palsy) weakens biceps flexion/supination; lower trunk C8–T1 injury (Klumpke) affects intrinsic hand muscles and may cause claw hand; thoracic outlet syndrome compresses lower trunk and subclavian vessels; long thoracic C5–C7 injury affects serratus anterior and causes scapular winging/inability to anchor the scapula. This supports the scapular motor-deficit option; the page does not use the exact word ‘protraction.’

C.text: Upper-extremity nerve table: median nerve injury can cause thenar/LOAF deficits and sensory loss involving the lateral 3½ fingers; carpal tunnel syndrome is a distal median-nerve lesion.

D.text: Upper-extremity nerve table: midshaft humeral fracture may injure radial nerve and cause wrist drop; wrist extension is needed for maximal grip strength.

E.text: Upper-extremity nerve table: ulnar neuropathy causes ulnar claw, impaired finger abduction/adduction, and sensory loss over the ulnar 1½ fingers including the hypothenar eminence.

F.text: Brachial-plexus lesions table/diagram: upper trunk C5–C6 injury (Erb palsy) weakens biceps flexion/supination; lower trunk C8–T1 injury (Klumpke) affects intrinsic hand muscles and may cause claw hand; thoracic outlet syndrome compresses lower trunk and subclavian vessels; long thoracic C5–C7 injury affects serratus anterior and causes scapular winging/inability to anchor the scapula. This supports the scapular motor-deficit option; the page does not use the exact word ‘protraction.’

自建题库/KAPLAN QBANK/ANATOMY/anatomy extra..fa_summary: First Aid's brachial plexus diagram and lesion table contrast upper-trunk Erb palsy with lower-trunk Klumpke palsy; the C8-T1 pattern matches the medial sensory loss and hand clawing here.

自建题库/KAPLAN QBANK/ANATOMY/anatomy extra..stem: A 16-year-old boy is brought to the emergency department after sustaining multiple knife wounds, including one into the axilla. Neurologic examination suggests an injury to the posterior cord of the brachial plexus. Further evaluation reveals no major vascular injury. Which of the following muscles is most likely to be paralyzed?
自建题库/KAPLAN QBANK/ANATOMY/anatomy extra..explanation: The posterior cord gives rise to the axillary and radial nerves. Of the listed muscles, deltoid is supplied by the axillary nerve and would be affected. Brachialis is mainly musculocutaneous; flexor digitorum superficialis and pronator teres are median-innervated; rhomboids are supplied by the dorsal scapular nerve.

choice_explanations.A: Incorrect: brachialis is chiefly supplied by musculocutaneous nerve (with a small radial contribution variably described).
choice_explanations.B: Correct: deltoid is supplied by the axillary nerve, a posterior-cord branch.
choice_explanations.C: Incorrect: flexor digitorum superficialis is supplied by the median nerve.
choice_explanations.D: Incorrect: pronator teres is supplied by the median nerve.
choice_explanations.E: Incorrect: rhomboids are supplied by the dorsal scapular nerve, usually arising from C5 root.

自建题库/KAPLAN QBANK/ANATOMY/anatomy extra..stem: A 17-year-old girl who is a soccer player is brought to the emergency department after a posterior dislocation of her right knee during a soccer game. On physical examination, there is significant swelling of the knee and significant bruising on the posterior aspect. The dislocation is reduced, but the pulses distal to the site of injury are not easily palpable. Angiograms of the lower extremities are shown. Which of the following vascular structures, indicated by arrows in the image, is most likely damaged in this patient?
自建题库/KAPLAN QBANK/ANATOMY/anatomy extra..explanation: Posterior knee dislocation can injure the popliteal artery because it is tethered proximally and distally around the knee. Posterior bruising and diminished distal pulses are red flags for this vascular injury. The arrows in the source angiogram indicate the popliteal artery at the knee.

choice_explanations.A: Incorrect: anterior tibial artery branches distal to the knee; the source arrows mark the vessel at the knee joint.
choice_explanations.B: Incorrect: fibular artery is a distal branch and is not the vessel indicated at the knee.
choice_explanations.C: Correct: popliteal artery is vulnerable to injury in knee dislocation.
choice_explanations.D: Incorrect: posterior tibial artery is distal to the popliteal artery bifurcation.
choice_explanations.E: Incorrect: femoral artery is proximal to the knee and not the vessel marked by the arrows.

自建题库/KAPLAN QBANK/ANATOMY/anatomy extra..stem: A 54-year-old woman is admitted to the intensive care unit because of sepsis secondary to a urinary tract infection. The decision is made to place a central line catheter in the lumen of the right internal jugular vein to better track hemodynamic information. A resident performs the procedure guided by ultrasound, but during the course of the procedure, inadvertently pierces through the vein and damages structures located posterior to the carotid sheath. Which of the following is most likely to occur?

options.text: Inability to abduct the right eye
Inability to close the right eye
Paralysis of the platysma muscle on the right side

自建题库/KAPLAN QBANK/ANATOMY/anatomy extra..explanation: The cervical sympathetic trunk lies posterior to the carotid sheath. Injury interrupts sympathetic supply to the ipsilateral head, causing Horner syndrome: miosis (constricted pupil), mild ptosis, and anhidrosis. The pupil constricts because the dilator pupillae loses sympathetic input.

choice_explanations.A: Correct: loss of sympathetic input causes ipsilateral miosis.
choice_explanations.B: Incorrect: dilation requires intact sympathetic activation of dilator pupillae.
choice_explanations.C: Incorrect: abduction is performed by lateral rectus (CN VI), not the cervical sympathetic trunk.
choice_explanations.D: Incorrect: eyelid closure is mediated by orbicularis oculi (CN VII).
choice_explanations.E: Incorrect: platysma is supplied by cervical branch of facial nerve.

A.text: Horner syndrome section: sympathetic denervation causes ipsilateral ptosis, miosis, and anhidrosis; the page diagrams the sympathetic pathway and identifies CN VI/lateral rectus separately.

B.text: Pupillary-control diagram/text: light in either eye activates bilateral Edinger–Westphal nuclei and constricts both pupils; optic-nerve afferent lesions cause a relative afferent pupillary defect.

C.text: Horner/ciliary sympathetic pathway is diagrammed; CN VI innervates lateral rectus, and CN VII is not the motor nerve for eye abduction.

D.text: Cranial-nerve table: CN IX monitors carotid body/sinus chemo- and baroreceptors; CN XI turns the head; CN XII moves the tongue; CN V carries facial/lower-jaw sensation; CN VII carries anterior-tongue taste and closes the eye; CN X supports talking and swallowing.

E.text: Pharyngeal-arch derivative table: CN VII (second arch) supplies muscles of facial expression, including platysma.

自建题库/KAPLAN QBANK/ANATOMY/anatomy extra..fa_summary: First Aid's Horner syndrome diagram and summary describe sympathetic-chain injury causing ipsilateral miosis, ptosis, and anhidrosis (p. 555).

自建题库/KAPLAN QBANK/ANATOMY/anatomy extra..stem: A 58-year-old man is brought to his general physician by family members because of recent cognitive changes. His family is concerned that he is no longer able to recognize common objects in his surroundings. Neurologic examination shows that when he is presented with a picture of a dog, he is able to copy the picture but is unable to recognize the animal as a dog. This finding is most likely caused by a lesion to which of the following areas?
自建题库/KAPLAN QBANK/ANATOMY/anatomy extra..explanation: This is visual agnosia: visual perception and copying are intact, but the patient cannot recognize a familiar object. Lesions of the temporo-occipital visual association cortex can cause this deficit. Prosopagnosia is a related visual agnosia specifically affecting face recognition.

choice_explanations.A: Incorrect: angular gyrus lesions can cause language/reading and calculation syndromes, not classic visual object agnosia.
choice_explanations.B: Incorrect: frontal eye field controls voluntary saccades.
choice_explanations.C: Incorrect: parieto-occipital association cortex integrates spatial/somatosensory and visual information; the source localizes this visual recognition deficit to temporo-occipital association cortex.
choice_explanations.D: Incorrect: precentral gyrus is primary motor cortex.
choice_explanations.E: Incorrect: prefrontal cortex supports executive function and behavior.
choice_explanations.F: Correct: temporo-occipital visual association cortex supports recognition of visually perceived objects.

自建题库/KAPLAN QBANK/ANATOMY/anatomy extra..stem: A newborn is born at 43 weeks' gestation after a difficult delivery complicated by breech presentation. External cephalic version was attempted prior to delivery but ultrasound showed no change in the position of the baby. The decision was made to attempt a breech delivery. Following delivery, physical examination shows an adducted and internally rotated shoulder with an extended elbow and pronated forearm. An x-ray of the arm and forearm does not show any abnormalities. Loss of innervation to which of the following muscles best accounts for both the extended elbow and pronated forearm?
自建题库/KAPLAN QBANK/ANATOMY/anatomy extra..explanation: The posture is Erb palsy from traction injury to the upper trunk (C5-C6) of the brachial plexus during delivery. Biceps brachii is weakened, impairing elbow flexion and forearm supination; the limb assumes the classic adducted, internally rotated shoulder with extended elbow and pronated forearm. Brachialis also flexes the elbow but does not supinate the forearm, so it does not explain both findings.

choice_explanations.A: Correct: biceps brachii flexes the elbow and supinates the forearm; C5-C6 injury weakens it.
choice_explanations.B: Incorrect: brachialis flexes the elbow but does not supinate the forearm.
choice_explanations.C: Incorrect: coracobrachialis acts at the shoulder, not elbow flexion or forearm supination.
choice_explanations.D: Incorrect: deltoid acts at the shoulder and cannot explain elbow extension plus pronation.
choice_explanations.E: Incorrect: pronator teres pronates the forearm; loss would tend toward reduced pronation, not the observed pronated posture.

This supports the scapular motor-deficit option; the page does not use the exact word ‘protraction.’

自建题库/KAPLAN QBANK/ANATOMY/MUSCLOSKELETAL.stem: A 46-year-old woman with a history of Lyme disease undergoes excision of a right Baker cyst. Three months later, she has decreased sensation over the dorsum of the foot, especially in the web space between the first and second toes. She trips while walking and has mild right foot drop. Dysfunction of which muscle most likely causes her motor symptoms?
自建题库/KAPLAN QBANK/ANATOMY/MUSCLOSKELETAL.explanation: Excision of a Baker cyst can injure or scar the common fibular nerve as it courses through the popliteal fossa. Its deep branch supplies the anterior leg compartment, including tibialis anterior, which dorsiflexes the ankle. Weak dorsiflexion causes foot drop and toe-catching; sensory loss in the first dorsal web space specifically points to the deep fibular nerve. The other listed muscles do not dorsiflex the ankle.

choice_explanations.A: Incorrect: flexor hallucis longus is a posterior-compartment muscle supplied by the tibial nerve; it flexes the great toe and assists plantar flexion.
choice_explanations.B: Incorrect: fibularis brevis is supplied by the superficial fibular nerve and everts the foot; it does not dorsiflex it.
choice_explanations.C: Incorrect: fibularis longus is also a superficial-fibular-nerve muscle that everts and plantar-flexes the foot.
choice_explanations.D: Correct: tibialis anterior is supplied by the deep fibular nerve and is a primary ankle dorsiflexor.
choice_explanations.E: Incorrect: tibialis posterior is supplied by the tibial nerve and primarily inverts and plantar-flexes the foot.

A.text: First Aid p.457 distinguishes tibial-nerve motor supply to foot flexors and plantar-flexion functions from common fibular nerve functions. A flexor hallucis longus deficit would impair toe flexion rather than produce the first-web-space sensory loss and dorsiflexion weakness in this vignette.

B.text: First Aid p.457 assigns fibularis (peroneus) longus and brevis to the superficial peroneal nerve. The superficial branch supplies most of the dorsum of the foot but spares the first web space; its injury chiefly weakens eversion, not tibialis-anterior dorsiflexion.

C.text: First Aid p.457 assigns fibularis (peroneus) longus and brevis to the superficial peroneal nerve. This explains eversion and much of dorsal-foot sensation, but not the first web-space sensory loss and dorsiflexion weakness that point to the deep branch.

D.text: First Aid p.457 identifies tibialis anterior as a deep peroneal motor target and the first web space as its sensory territory; common fibular injury can cause foot drop. This directly matches the vignette and the correct answer.

E.text: First Aid p.457 contrasts tibial-nerve plantar-flexor/foot-flexor function with common fibular dorsiflexor function. A tibialis-posterior problem would not explain first-web-space sensory loss with foot drop.

自建题库/KAPLAN QBANK/ANATOMY/MUSCLOSKELETAL.fa_summary: First Aid 2026's lower-extremity nerve table links common fibular nerve injury, including compression by a Baker cyst, with dorsal-foot sensory loss and foot drop; the deep fibular branch supplies the anterior compartment (printed p. 457).

自建题库/KAPLAN QBANK/ANATOMY/MUSCLOSKELETAL.stem: A 35-year-old man sustains a humeral fracture during a rugby game. Two months later, he has difficulty abducting the arm, especially beyond the first 15 degrees, and decreased sensation over the lateral shoulder. Where is the fracture most likely located?
自建题库/KAPLAN QBANK/ANATOMY/MUSCLOSKELETAL.explanation: This is an axillary nerve lesion. The nerve wraps around the surgical neck of the humerus and supplies the deltoid and teres minor, as well as skin over the lateral shoulder. The supraspinatus initiates the first 15 degrees of abduction; the deltoid abducts the arm thereafter, explaining the deficit beyond 15 degrees. A midshaft fracture more typically injures the radial nerve and causes wrist/finger extension weakness.

choice_explanations.A: Incorrect: the anatomical neck is within the shoulder-joint capsule; it is not the characteristic site for axillary nerve injury.
choice_explanations.B: Incorrect: a lateral epicondyle fracture can affect structures near the elbow, not the axillary nerve or lateral shoulder sensation.
choice_explanations.C: Incorrect: a medial epicondyle fracture may injure the ulnar nerve and cause medial-hand symptoms.
choice_explanations.D: Incorrect: a midshaft humeral fracture can injure the radial nerve, causing wrist drop and posterior-limb sensory loss.
choice_explanations.E: Correct: the axillary nerve passes around the surgical neck; injury weakens deltoid-mediated abduction and reduces lateral-shoulder sensation.

A.text: First Aid p.450 associates axillary-nerve injury with a surgical-neck fracture and loss of shoulder abduction beyond 15 degrees. The vignette's deltoid-pattern deficit supports the surgical-neck option rather than an anatomical-neck location.

B.text: The 2026 First Aid p.450 nerve table does not identify a lateral-epicondyle fracture as a cause of this deltoid/lateral-shoulder sensory pattern; it specifically links that pattern to axillary nerve injury at the surgical neck.

C.text: First Aid p.450 links medial-epicondyle fractures to ulnar-nerve injury, which causes ulnar-hand sensory and intrinsic-hand deficits rather than loss of deltoid-mediated shoulder abduction.

D.text: First Aid p.450 associates humeral midshaft fractures with radial-nerve injury and wrist/finger-extension deficits. It does not match the axillary-nerve pattern of lateral-shoulder sensory loss and impaired abduction beyond 15 degrees.

E.text: First Aid p.450 explicitly links a surgical-neck fracture to axillary-nerve injury, flattened deltoid, loss of shoulder abduction beyond 15 degrees, and reduced sensation over the deltoid/lateral arm. This is the matching option.

自建题库/KAPLAN QBANK/ANATOMY/MUSCLOSKELETAL.fa_summary: First Aid's upper-extremity nerve table associates a humeral surgical-neck fracture with axillary nerve injury, flattened deltoid, impaired abduction beyond 15 degrees, and lateral-arm sensory loss (printed p. 450).

自建题库/KAPLAN QBANK/ANATOMY/MUSCLOSKELETAL.stem: A 55-year-old woman with depression is admitted after deep lacerations of the distal wrist and palm. Several weeks later, she has hand weakness and numbness with flattening of the thenar eminence. Which additional finding is most likely?

options.text: Loss of sensation over the palmar aspect of the fifth digit
Weakness of the first and second lumbricals

自建题库/KAPLAN QBANK/ANATOMY/MUSCLOSKELETAL.explanation: Flattening of the thenar eminence after a distal wrist/palm laceration indicates injury to the median nerve or its recurrent motor branch. The median nerve supplies the first and second lumbricals and thenar muscles. Pronation is mediated by forearm muscles proximal to the wrist and should be spared by a distal lesion. Fifth-digit sensation and thumb adduction are ulnar-nerve functions; thumb extension is radial-nerve mediated.

choice_explanations.A: Incorrect: palmar sensation over the fifth digit is supplied by the ulnar nerve.
choice_explanations.B: Incorrect: pronation is produced by pronator teres and pronator quadratus in the forearm, proximal to the wrist laceration.
choice_explanations.C: Incorrect: thumb adduction is primarily performed by adductor pollicis, supplied by the deep branch of the ulnar nerve.
choice_explanations.D: Incorrect: thumb extension is performed by radial-nerve-innervated posterior forearm muscles.
choice_explanations.E: Correct: the first and second lumbricals are median-nerve supplied and may be weakened by a distal median-nerve injury.

A.text: First Aid p.450 describes ulnar-nerve sensory loss over the ulnar 1½ digits. This is a possible ulnar-nerve finding but is not the additional finding expected from a distal median-nerve injury with thenar atrophy.

B.text: First Aid p.450 outlines median-nerve deficits and distinguishes proximal from distal lesions. The page does not specifically name pronation, so this option's exact movement is not directly detailed there; a distal wrist/palm lesion is too distal to denervate proximal pronator muscles.

C.text: First Aid p.450 assigns thumb adduction to the ulnar nerve. Therefore thumb-adduction weakness would suggest an ulnar-nerve lesion, not the median-nerve lesion signaled by thenar atrophy.

D.text: First Aid p.450 associates radial-nerve injury with loss of wrist and finger extension. Thumb extension is also a radial-nerve function, so it is not the expected deficit from a distal median-nerve/palmar lesion.

E.text: First Aid p.450 lists the lateral two lumbricals among median-nerve functions; p.454 illustrates hand deformities from median and ulnar lesions. A distal median lesion can weaken the first and second lumbricals, matching this option.

自建题库/KAPLAN QBANK/ANATOMY/MUSCLOSKELETAL.fa_summary: First Aid's hand-muscle table identifies the first two lumbricals and most thenar muscles as median-nerve supplied; distal median injury produces thenar weakness/atrophy, whereas ulnar muscles control thumb adduction (printed p. 452).
